commits.messageBody:
…tside its own connect flow

--port=0 gives the local engine a fresh OS-assigned port every restart.
Since #1413/#1492 the extension syncs that port into the workspace .env on
each successful connect, but that only helps a script reading .env from the
SAME workspace at its own startup -- a long-running script that outlives an
engine restart, or any process not tied to that specific workspace, has no
way to notice or discover the new port short of grep-matching `lsof`.

Adds a small, fixed, workspace-independent connection discovery file
(<user config dir>/engine/connection.json -- the same directory
version.json/engine-<pid>.pid already live in) that EngineLocal writes when
the engine becomes ready and removes when that same process exits (guarded
by a stored pid, so one window's stop can't clobber a different window's
live entry). apiKey is hardcoded to the local-mode default ('MYAPIKEY'):
EngineLocal only knows the port it started on, not which connection-group
config ultimately drives the client's actual auth, and this file is a
discovery convenience, not an auth source of truth.

RocketRideClient() (Python SDK) now checks this file as a fallback when no
explicit uri is given and ROCKETRIDE_URI isn't set via env/.env, verifying
the recorded pid is still alive before trusting a stale entry left behind
by a crash. An explicit uri/ROCKETRIDE_URI always wins; this is only
consulted as a last resort before the cloud default.

Scope, deliberately: a single "last-connected" file, not a registry of
every concurrently-running local engine across multiple VS Code windows.
For the reported problem -- one developer, one local engine, losing track
of it across reloads -- that's exactly the right answer; disambiguating
several simultaneous local engines is a separate, harder problem nobody
asked for here.

Fixes #1851
